summary.headline: Hindalco Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 52% YoY to ₹13,869 crore, with copper EBITDA a record ₹1,673 crore including one-offs of ~₹350–400 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated EBITDA was ₹13,869 crore (+52% YoY) and consolidated PAT ₹7,534 crore (+59% YoY), led by India aluminium upstream (EBITDA ₹7,009 crore, +55%, ₹2,125/t) and a record copper EBITDA. Management said roughly ₹350–400 crore of copper EBITDA was non-recurring, with normalised copper EBITDA guided at ~₹1,200–1,300 crore per quarter. Aluminium cost of production rose ~5% QoQ on coal, and Novelis guidance of $600/t long-term EBITDA was unchanged with Bay Minette first cold roll coil in September. Capex was ₹20,719 crore (+83% YoY) against operating cash flow of ₹23,322 crore.

financial_highlights.value: ₹1,673 crore (record); metal shipments 116 kt; CCR 96 kt

segments.name: India upstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments +1% YoY, revenue +33% YoY, EBITDA ₹7,009 crore (+55%), ₹2,125/t, with higher net premium from exports to high-premium markets and better VAP pricing. Q2 cost of production rose ~5% QoQ on coal.

segments.name: India downstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments +6% YoY to 119 kt; EBITDA ₹329 crore (+26%), $289/t, driven by product mix and premiumisation.

segments.name: India copper
segments.commentary: Record EBITDA ₹1,673 crore (+164% YoY) on metal shipments of 116 kt (+2%) and CCR 96 kt (stable). Sulphuric acid realisation ~₹16,000/t vs ~₹7,000/t a year ago; ~₹350–400 crore one-offs in the quarter; underlying run-rate guided at ~₹1,200–1,300 crore.

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Oswego hot mill production normalised; cumulative insurance recoveries of $519 million through September 2026. Long-term EBITDA guidance $600/t unchanged; 600 kt Bay Minette first cold roll coil in September, commercial shipments from Q1 FY28. Management expects net debt/EBITDA to reach ~4x in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Aluminium cost of production expected to stay ~5% higher in Q3 vs Q2 due to coal; Q4 expected to ease as coal availability improves.
Copper underlying quarterly EBITDA guided at ~₹1,200–1,300 crore, driven by sulphuric acid, precious metals and downstream pricing.

Novelis: tariff headwinds to fall to a marginal level by Q4; Young's strike impact ~$20 million in Q2 and similar in Q3; further ~$47 million insurance recovery to fall into EBITDA by fiscal year end; shipments to pick up from Q4.
Hedging: ~29% of aluminium for rest of FY27 at $3,000/t and 21% of currency at ₹93/$; FY28 ~26% hedged at $3,168/t.

Capex: ~₹12,000 crore in FY27; FY28 substantially higher (figure to be given in February); FY28–29 to remain high. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA to be kept around 2x; Novelis to deleverage to 2.5–2.8x over two years.
Pot relining capitalisation adds ~₹130 crore to EBITDA and ~₹130 crore to depreciation per quarter going forward.
Alumina sales of ~194 kt in Q2; Q3 expected at 190–210 kt. Alumina index currently above $350/t, expected closer to $400 next year.
capex_capacity: Commissioning: Aditya copper recycling plant (Pakhajan) December 2026; Aditya alumina refinery and first 180 kt aditya smelter line December 2027; next Aditya line and copper smelter December 2028.
Doubling upstream capacity remains the goal; Mahan 370 kt expansion in ECE/licensing stage; Mahan can add a further 720 kt; Aditya has no further smelter land after the 360 kt expansion.
Downstream: copper recycling expansion from 50 kt to 150 kt planned; Aditya can add a 170 kt cold mill; extrusion projects at Kuppam and Silvassa; target four-fold downstream EBITDA by FY30.
Captive coal: Bandha in high stripping phase, first coal expected in H2 FY28; Chakla coal expected around mid-FY28.
Over ₹50,000 crore of expansion under execution in India, another ~₹50,000 crore under evaluation; ~₹20,000 crore of the first tranche spent by year end.
Renewables: 643 MW at end-Q2, rising to 884 MW by exit FY27, plus 125 MW RE-TC capacity.
demand_pricing: Global aluminium deficit around 0.8 Mt for calendar 2026 per management estimate; Chinese output +3% YoY to ~11 Mt; ex-China output -6% to ~8 Mt (Mozal closure, Middle East disruption).
Global consumption +1% YoY to ~19 Mt; China +4% to ~12 Mt; ex-China -2% to ~7 Mt.
India aluminium demand Q2 FY27 ~1.7 Mt, +6% YoY, led by automotive; India expected to grow ~7–8% p.a.
India refined copper demand -3% YoY to 388 kt; copper concentrate TCRCs at minus $48 to minus $58/t spot.
MJP premium was ~$270/t in Q3, expected $200–250/t in Q4 per management; down more than $100/t from peak.
Management's LME outlook for next year: consensus $2,600–2,800/t; internal IRR planning uses ~$2,600/t. Highest-cost Indonesian cash cost ~$2,000–2,200/t.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for the ₹50,000 crore expansion pipeline under evaluation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focused on first-tranche projects (Pakhajan copper recycling Dec 2026, Aditya alumina and smelter line Dec 2027); a new project is to start about every 1.5 years, with Mahan next and gated by execution capacity and balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Aluminium cost trajectory and captive coal timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 costs rose ~5% QoQ, with Q3 also ~5% higher on northern-plant coal shortfalls; Q4 expected to ease. Bandha coal in H2 FY28, Chakla around mid-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Sulphuric acid realisation and share of copper EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation ~₹16,000/t vs ~₹7,000/t a year ago; ~300 kt per quarter. About 40–50% of copper-business EBITDA is said to come from by-products, with the rest from copper products.

qa_highlights.question: Novelis volume and margin guidance given tariffs and scrap spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited specific swing factors: tariffs to fall to marginal levels by Q4, Young's strike impact ~$20 million each in Q2 and Q3, and ~$47 million of insurance recovery by fiscal year end; shipments expected to pick up from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was upstream EBITDA better than expected despite LME decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher net premium from exports to high-premium markets and better pricing on value-added products such as conductors and cables.

qa_highlights.question: Copper one-offs and sustainable run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹350–400 crore non-repeatable (slag sales accruals, derivative effects, extra precious-metal sales); underlying run-rate ~₹1,200–1,300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and pot relining impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Pot relining capitalisation adds ~₹130 crore to EBITDA and ~₹130 crore to depreciation per quarter, with Q2 including some Q1 catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: Net cash and debt position in India?
qa_highlights.answer: India has ~₹16,000 crore treasury, ~₹6,000–7,000 crore long-term loans, net cash ~₹9,000 crore; India net debt/EBITDA -0.35x.

qa_highlights.question: Royalty and spend to date on the ₹50,000 crore programme?
qa_highlights.answer: Royalty ~$11 million paid until the ₹225 crore cap; about ₹20,000 crore of the ₹50,000 crore spent so far (expected by year end).

risks_watch: Coal supply in northern India: ~5% aluminium cost pressure through Q3 FY27 until Chakla/Bandha coal starts.
LME and MJP sensitivity: ~$2,600–2,800/t assumed for next year; Indonesian supply additions and Middle East events could move prices quickly.
Copper earnings quality: ~₹350–400 crore one-offs in Q2; normalised ₹1,200–1,300 crore depends on sulphuric acid pricing, which has been very high.
Novelis: tariffs, strike impact, customer supply-chain normalisation and deleveraging to ~4x by Q4 FY27.
Execution capacity and capex peak in FY28–29; net debt/EBITDA target ~2x consolidated.

So Q2 costs were up roughly 5% above Q1.

So we will you know LMEs can swing up and down but we will be the last man standing so yes we think that taking advantage of the backward integration of bauxite and coal is the reason why we should do the investment there can be some years where it goes down but the fundamental demand of aluminum we think the long-term trend is good.

I think that you know for us let me be one thing is clear the copper concentrate availability is tight but for people like us we are now very comfortable because we have got large miners with which we have long-term contracts so we have no problem in getting the concentrate.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the India upstream and copper franchise, with a firm line that Novelis swing factors are quantified and manageable. Noticeably cautious on LME direction, calling 2026-28 prices a view subject to geopolitical swings, and reticent on copper EBITDA breakup and capex quantum for FY28, deferring the number to February.

adds.what: Aditya alumina refinery and first 180 kt Aditya smelter line
Renewables: 643 MW at end-Q2 rising to 884 MW by exit FY27

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; copper underlying EBITDA guided at ~₹1,200–1,300 cr/quarter and Novelis $600/t held, with ~₹12,000 cr FY27 capex and Aditya/Mahan capacity timelines (Dec 2026 to Dec 2027+) giving partial backing, while Q3 aluminium cost guided ~5% higher QoQ on coal.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Copper underlying EBITDA guided ~₹1,200–1,300 cr/qtr vs ₹1,673 cr reported (₹350–400 cr one-offs), and Q3 aluminium cost ~5% higher QoQ on coal, easing in Q4; Novelis $600/t held and pot relining adds ~₹130 cr EBITDA/qtr.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pakhajan copper recycling commissioning Dec 2026, renewables rising from 643 MW to 884 MW by exit FY27, and Bay Minette first cold roll coil already in September; Aditya alumina and 180 kt smelter line follow Dec 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Novelis shipments to pick up from Q4 after Oswego normalisation and tariffs falling to marginal levels; India aluminium demand +6% YoY in Q2 and expected to grow ~7–8% p.a.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex ~₹12,000 cr in FY27 with FY28 'substantially higher' (to be quantified in February); ~₹50,000 cr under evaluation with a new project starting about every 1.5 years and Mahan next, and Aditya has no further smelter land after the 360 kt expansion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Upstream EBITDA beat on export premiums, but management guides copper underlying to ₹1,200–1,300 cr and expects MJP premium to fall to $200–250/t in Q4 from ~$270/t in Q3, limiting upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Aluminium cost ~5% higher in Q3 on coal shortfall, Young's strike ~$20 mn impact each in Q2 and Q3, and copper one-offs of ₹350–400 cr will not recur, with sulphuric acid at ~₹16,000/t vs ~₹7,000/t a year ago.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bay Minette 600 kt cold roll coil with commercial shipments from Q1 FY28, and Pakhajan copper recycling plant (Dec 2026) adds recycling capacity from 50 kt toward 150 kt.

rows.label: Novelis deleveraging to ~4x by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management expects consolidated net debt/EBITDA to reach ~4x in Q4 FY27 from 1.8x in Sept 2026, with Novelis deleveraging to 2.5–2.8x over two years; ~$47 mn insurance recovery falls into EBITDA by year end.

rows.label: Captive coal start (Bandha, Chakla)
rows.why: Bandha first coal expected H2 FY28 and Chakla around mid-FY28; until then northern coal shortfall keeps aluminium cost ~5% higher through Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Global aluminium deficit tightening
rows.why: Management estimates a ~0.8 Mt global aluminium deficit for CY2026 as ex-China output falls ~6% to ~8 Mt (Mozal closure, Middle East disruption) while ex-China consumption falls ~2% to ~7 Mt.

tone.note: Management was confident on India upstream, copper and Novelis swing factors being quantified, but cautious on LME direction and deferred FY28 capex quantum and copper EBITDA breakup to February; analysts pushed on the sustainability of copper one-offs and the FY28 capex number.
